title: REPORT on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy – annual report 2025
part_text: 34. Stresses that a strong transatlantic partnership with the United States and Canada within NATO forms the core of the European security architecture; expresses concern, in this context, about the fact that certain elements of the new US National Security Strategy fall significantly short in adequately addressing the threat posed by Russia, in particular for European and hence also US security; regrets, furthermore, the National Security Strategy’s flawed assessment of the EU as a political system; strongly disagrees with the characterisation of migration as one of Europe’s main problems and risks, and that EU activities undermine political liberty; disagrees that international relations should be based on spheres of influence and that large countries should share power in any way in each hemisphere; condemns any attempts to influence or undermine democratic processes in the EU, including through disinformation, economic coercion, political pressure or external interference, and stresses the importance of safeguarding the integrity of EU institutions and decision-making; considers that the National Security Strategy further reinforces the imperative for Europe to advance its strategic autonomy, reduce dependencies, and diversify partnerships;
